summary: A choice the size of a card — a plan, a schedule, a template, each with a sentence. A real Radio inside a RadioGroup, a real Checkbox inside a CheckboxGroup or alone; its label is stretched over the tile, so the whole card is the target. The title is the name; the description is read after it.
useWhen: each option needs a sentence or a detail to be chosen well — what a plan includes, what a schedule costs
there are a handful of options, two to six, worth seeing side by side

useInstead.when: the options are short labels that need no explanation
useInstead.why: a column of radios is denser and quicker to scan than a grid of cards

useInstead.when: more than about six options, or a list that grows
useInstead.why: a grid of tiles for twenty options is a wall of cards

useInstead.when: the card leads somewhere, or holds actions
useInstead.why: a tile is one control and must hold nothing interactive

composition.note: Inside a RadioGroup the tiles are radios — one choice; inside a CheckboxGroup, checkboxes — several. The group's label, description, isRequired, isInvalid and errorMessage apply as they do to Radio and Checkbox, and the tiles wrap into a grid. Alone, a tile is a checkbox with `isSelected` and `onSelectionChange`. Put links — "Compare plans" — beside the group, not in a tile.
composition.example: <RadioGroup label="Plan" value={plan} onChange={setPlan}><SelectableTile value="team" title="Team" description="Up to 20 agents.">€49 a month</SelectableTile></RadioGroup>

requires: `title` — the option's name, short: it is the input's accessible name
a group label on the RadioGroup or CheckboxGroup — the question the tiles answer
guarantees: it is a native radio or checkbox: arrow keys move between radios, Space toggles a checkbox, and a form submits its value
the whole tile is the target, through the input's own label
the description and extra detail are read after the name, through aria-describedby
the group's help or error is read on each tile, as on Radio and Checkbox
selected thickens the border and fills the indicator — not a colour change alone
a keyboard focus ring goes round the whole tile
the icon is hidden from assistive tech
notes: nothing inside a tile may be interactive — the whole tile is one control
the tiles wrap into a grid 14rem and up, so a phone gets one column

antiPatterns.why: a clickable card is not a radio: it is not grouped, arrow keys do nothing, and a form does not submit it

antiPatterns.dont: a "Learn more" link inside a tile
antiPatterns.why: the whole tile is the control; a link on top of it is a second target in the same place
